title: Conquering Persia
objective: After this level you can trace Alexander's campaign against Persia.
summary: From 334 to 330 BCE Alexander crossed into Asia, beat Persia at the Granicus, Issus and Gaugamela, and burned Persepolis.

cards.headline: In 334 BCE a young king crossed into Asia to take on Persia.
cards.body: He brought about 30,000 infantry and more than 5,000 cavalry. Four years later, the Persian king was dead. Here’s the road.

cards.headline: First stop: Troy
cards.body: Alexander crossed the Dardanelles, and before his first battle he visited Troy. Yes, Level 5’s Troy, near the Dardanelles. Plutarch says he anointed Achilles’ gravestone with oil and ran a race by it with his companions. A general heading to war, pausing at the setting of his favorite book.

events.label: Wins his first battle, at the Granicus River
Beats Darius III at Issus; Darius flees
Storms Tyre; Egypt surrenders without a fight
Wins the decisive battle, at Gaugamela
Burns Xerxes’ palace; Darius is killed by his own men

cards.headline: Endings, real and legendary
cards.body: At Persepolis Alexander burned the palace of Xerxes, a sign that the Greek war of revenge on Persia was over. Some endings are harder to pin down. Legend said whoever loosed the Gordian knot would rule Asia, and most ancient writers say Alexander simply cut it with his sword. It may never have happened. It’s still a great story.

cards.headline: Persia falls
learned: Crossed into Asia in 334 BCE, via Troy
